title: The model house
units: metres; x east, y north; level = storey, 4 m each
rule: Ask what happens to the weights, and you know where you are: before the house (garden), being learned (below ground), used once (ground floor), changed after training (first floor), frozen while the words change (second floor), scored by the world (yard), read only (tower).

floors.name: The old garden
floors.reason: Before the house: the classic methods. It lies beyond the output balcony, so the balcony looks back at where the walk began; the first learning machine stands farthest out.

floors.name: The cellar
floors.reason: Weights being learned. Entered from the garden under the balcony, where the loss is computed; walked west, the way the gradient flows, so it ends under the gate, the last thing the gradient reaches.

floors.name: The ground floor
floors.reason: Weights used: one forward pass. The south row reads text in, west to east; the north row is the way back, where each written token returns to the gate.

floors.name: The footings
floors.reason: How big to build: loss against size, data and compute. Below the cellar because every floor stands on it.

floors.name: The first floor
floors.reason: Weights changed after training: fine-tuning, what that forgets, choices, and making the model smaller.

floors.name: The second floor
floors.reason: Weights frozen: only the words going in or coming out change. Examples, steps, instructions, fetched pages, tools.

floors.name: The yard
floors.reason: Outside the model: a score from the world decides, a reward or a program that checks.

floors.name: The tower
floors.reason: Weights read, never changed: looking inside. The higher you climb, the harder the question; the top asks whether any of it is real.

halls.note: Garden path; its west end drops by steps into the cellar.
Foot of the garden steps, under the balcony: where the loss is computed and the backward pass begins.
The gradient channel: gold water running west, under the residual stream.
Stair core beside the gate, from the footings to the second floor.
The residual stream: a channel of blue water from the gate to the balcony; every ground-floor room pours into it.
The output balcony, looking east over the old garden.
Outside stair from the workshop of hands down to the yard path.
Yard path along the south wall, walked west.

objects.idea: Rosenblatt's rule: on each mistake, add the point to the weights or subtract it, by its label; a right answer changes nothing.
objects.image: A garden rake on a string line lunges at every plant on the wrong side and drags the string toward it, then rests.

objects.idea: If some line separates the data with margin γ, the mistakes stop within (R/γ)².
objects.image: A tally post with only so many notches: the wider the gap between the two dashed strings, the fewer the notches, and the rake must stop when they run out.

objects.idea: No line splits XOR; one hidden layer that bends the plane lets a line work again.
objects.image: Four beds in a checker of blue and gold; the string spins forever until the bed folds like a cloth and the string lies flat between.

objects.idea: Least squares is a projection: the fit lies in the column space and the residual stands at a right angle to it; by gradient descent it explodes past a learning rate you can predict.
objects.image: A sundial: the shadow is the fit, the upright pin the residual. A ball hopping toward the shadow's tip lands on it; make each hop too long and it bounds off the dial.

formation.new: Points on a tilted plane in 3-D; one target point above drops a plumb line to its foot, with a right-angle tick; then a ball steps toward the foot and overshoots when the rate passes the bound.

objects.idea: Ridge: add a penalty on the size of the weights, (XᵀX + λI)w = Xᵀy, and two near-copy features stop cancelling in huge opposite weights.
objects.image: Two stakes pulling the string in opposite directions with all their might, until a spring between them makes both relax.

objects.idea: Bayes as odds: posterior odds are prior odds times the likelihood ratio, so a 96%-sensitive test can leave you 95% likely to be healthy.
objects.image: A hive with one queen among thousands of bees; a sieve catches the queen and a crowd of workers, and the workers win.

objects.idea: Naive Bayes assumes the features are independent given the class: closed form, cheap, and wrong in a known way.
objects.image: Garden gnomes who each vote on the flower alone, never looking at one another.

formation.new: Two tilted clouds; each gets an upright, axis-aligned ellipse that ignores the tilt; the straight cut they give cannot follow the tilt of the clouds.

objects.idea: k-NN labels a point by its nearest neighbours; 1-NN error lies between the Bayes error and twice it (Cover-Hart).
objects.image: A newcomer on a bench turns to the five nearest trees and takes their vote; two fences beside the bench mark the Bayes error and twice it.

objects.idea: PCA by power iteration: multiply any arrow by the covariance again and again and it turns to the main axis; deflate to find the next.
objects.image: A weather vane that, each time the wind blows, swings closer to the orchard's long row.

objects.idea: k-means sums a cloud up with a few centres: assign each point, move each centre to its points' mean, repeat; a moving average over small batches can shake a centre out of a bad spot, if the batches are noisy enough.
objects.image: Three scarecrows that each walk to the middle of the birds they scare, until none moves.

formation.new: Three blobs of points; three gold centres step toward their cluster means each round, with the dividing lines redrawn; one run uses a jittering moving average.

objects.idea: The hard-margin SVM cuts the widest gap; only the support vectors get a vote, read off α.
objects.image: A plank laid across the pond as wide as it will go, held up by three stones that touch its edges; the rest of the stones could vanish.

objects.idea: The kernel trick: lift the points so a flat cut works, and compute the inner product without ever doing the lift.
objects.image: Two rings of lily pads; a swell lifts the outer ring high and the inner one hardly at all, and a flat sheet of glass slides between them.

formation.new: Concentric rings in a plane; each point rises in z by x²+y² so the outer ring lifts above the inner; a horizontal plane of faint points cuts between the rings.

objects.idea: A Hopfield network stores patterns as valleys of an energy; updates only go downhill and repair a corrupted input; it holds about 0.138·N patterns.
objects.image: A stone basin carved with hollows; a chipped marble dropped in rolls into the nearest hollow and comes out whole.

objects.idea: The modern Hopfield update Xᵀsoftmax(βXξ) lines up term by term with attention, softmax(QKᵀ/√d)V.
objects.image: A torch from the atrium stands by the basin: shine it on the hollows and the best match flashes back, the same trick as the mirrors indoors.

objects.idea: Double descent: test error peaks where parameters equal data points, p = n, then falls again as the fitter picks the smallest-norm fit; here it never gets back below the first dip.
objects.image: A footbridge dips, climbs to a sharp hump at the pond's neck, then comes down again, but lands higher than its first dip.

objects.idea: Every operation you apply records a node; the forward pass builds a graph.
objects.image: Every word you say in the echo room is carved as a stone on the floor, joined by string to the words it came from.

objects.idea: Reverse mode is message passing: each node multiplies the slope it receives by its own local slope and passes it back.
objects.image: Shout at the last stone and the echo runs back along the strings, louder or softer at each stone.

objects.idea: Run backward in reverse topological order, so each node has all its gradient before it passes any on.
objects.image: Numbered stepping stones; the echo may only leave a stone once every string into it has rung.

objects.idea: Gradient checking: compare each slope with a finite difference to catch a wrong derivative.
objects.image: A pair of scales by the door weighs every slope against a nudge of the input; a wrong one tips over.

formation.new: Pairs of points, one per parameter: the analytic slope and the finite-difference slope sit together; one pair splits apart and turns gold.

objects.idea: With this engine a small MLP walks downhill on its loss to 100% on two moons' 100 training points.
objects.image: A ball rolls down the floor of the echo room into a bowl, step by step against the slope.

objects.idea: A network is weighted sums, each followed by a bend; derive each layer's forward and backward by hand.
objects.image: The mill's stacked grindstones, each one tilted, each one followed by a hinge.

objects.idea: Fused softmax and cross-entropy: the gradient on the scores is simply p minus the one-hot answer.
objects.image: A row of sacks on a scale; the right sack is pulled down by exactly how short it fell.

formation.new: Bars of a softmax with the right class marked gold; arrows on each bar show p − y, down on the true class, up on the rest.

objects.idea: The training loop: split, batch, forward, backward, step, measure, every epoch.
objects.image: A waterwheel with six buckets, each painted with one step, turning round and round.

formation.new: Six stations on a ring; points ride the ring in batches, pausing at each station; a counter of epochs ticks on each turn.

objects.idea: It overfits: training loss keeps falling while held-out loss turns up; stop at its lowest point.
objects.image: Two water marks on the mill wall: one keeps sinking, the other bottoms out and starts to rise.

objects.idea: Make deterministic, disjoint train, validation and test splits, by whatever unit could leak; open the test set once.
objects.image: Three locked chests; the test chest has one key, which breaks in the lock after one use.

objects.idea: Leakage is the fastest route to a fake win: duplicates across splits inflate the score.
objects.image: A drip from the training chest into the test chest, and a trophy that grows as the puddle grows.

objects.idea: The confusion matrix is the primitive: accuracy, precision, recall, specificity and F1 all come from its four counts.
objects.image: Four drawers in the vault, labelled by the two ways to be right and the two ways to be wrong.

objects.idea: A threshold is a product decision: moving it trades one kind of error for the other.
objects.image: A sliding bar across the vault door; push it and coins fall from one drawer into the other.

objects.idea: Calibration: does 0.8 sure mean right eight times in ten? Measure it, do not assume it.
objects.image: A shelf of jars labelled 10% to 90%, each filled to how often it was right; the honest jars match their labels.

objects.idea: One aggregate can hide a slice that got worse; compare slices, with error bars.
objects.image: A good average on the front of the vault door, and behind it one small drawer marked low-light that is half empty.

objects.idea: SGD, momentum and Adam as update rules: momentum keeps speed through flats, Adam scales each step per weight.
objects.image: Three balls race down the sunken floor: one plods, one swings with momentum, one adjusts its stride on every tile.

objects.idea: The learning rate decides a lot, and the best one depends on the optimiser.
objects.image: A ball thrown too hard bounces from wall to wall of the slope and never settles.

objects.idea: Linear warmup then cosine decay: start gently, then let the rate fall smoothly to zero.
objects.image: A dimmer switch on the wall that slowly brightens, then fades along a smooth curve.

formation.new: A learning-rate curve that rises in a straight line then falls as half a cosine; a gold point rides it while the ball's steps lengthen and shorten.

objects.idea: Slice the loss along filter-normalised directions; the top Hessian eigenvalue measures how sharp the bottom is.
objects.image: A surveyor cuts a slice through the floor and holds it up: a sharp V or a wide U.

objects.idea: Grokking: the network fits its training set long before it finds the rule; weight decay made the late jump happen in this run.
objects.image: A clock on the far wall stays wrong for hours, then suddenly shows the right time; a small weight on its pendulum is what does it.

objects.idea: Self-supervised learning: the data supplies its own targets; hide part and predict it back.
objects.image: Blindfolded statues whose hands try to trace the half of the picture that is covered.

objects.idea: SimCLR: two crops of one image should land close together, and crops of others far away.
objects.image: Two halves of one torn photo pulled together across the room by a spring.

objects.idea: A JEPA predicts the latent of the hidden block, not its pixels.
objects.image: A statue points at a sealed box and names what it holds, without ever drawing it.

formation.new: A context cloud and a separate target cloud; a predictor arrow lands on the target cloud's centre in latent space, never on its pixels.

objects.idea: Collapse: map every input to one point and the JEPA loss is perfect and worthless.
objects.image: All the statues turn and point at the same nail in the wall.

objects.idea: Block collapse with stop-gradient, an EMA target, a variance term or SIGReg; measure it by spread and effective rank.
objects.image: A sheepdog that runs round the points and keeps them spread in a round flock.

objects.idea: Backprop keeps every layer's activations for the backward pass, so its memory grows with depth and batch.
objects.image: A porter who must carry a copy of every room he passed through, his pile growing at each door.

formation.new: A stack of layers; each leaves a pile of points behind as the forward pass goes up; a gold bar of memory grows with depth; checkpointing keeps only some piles and recomputes the rest.

objects.idea: MeZO: nudge every weight along one random direction both ways; two forward passes give the slope along it.
objects.image: A blindfolded walker taps the floor one step left and one step right and leans toward the lower tap.

objects.idea: Forward-forward and Mono-Forward: each layer learns from a goal of its own, with no error sent down.
objects.image: Each layer of the room has its own little target pinned on its wall and its own dart.

formation.new: Separate layer rings, each with its own gold target; points in each ring move toward their target with no arrows between rings.

objects.idea: Predictive coding: layers trade prediction errors; the error fades with depth.
objects.image: Whispers passed down a line of people get quieter at every ear.

formation.new: Layer columns with an error bar beside each; the bars shrink from output to input over the inference steps.

objects.idea: Read a memory claim with its meter: the memory a rule saves is not the memory its optimiser costs.
objects.image: Two gauges by the door, one for tensors alive, one for the whole process, often disagreeing.

formation.new: Two vertical bar meters per rule side by side, tensors alive against process memory.

objects.idea: Text must become numbers: start from single bytes or characters.
objects.image: At the gate, a sentence is pulled apart into loose letters that rattle into a tray.

objects.idea: BPE merges the commonest adjacent pair into one symbol, again and again.
objects.image: A gatekeeper who glues the two letters he sees side by side most often into one tile.

objects.idea: The list of merges is the whole tokenizer; frequent pieces become tokens.
objects.image: The gatekeeper's ledger of glued pairs, which is all he needs to chop any new text.

objects.idea: Byte-level BPE round-trips exactly: decode(encode(text)) gives back the text.
objects.image: Tiles run through the gate and back out, and the sentence that leaves is letter for letter the one that came in.

formation.new: Token chips merge into longer chips, then unmerge back to the same characters in the same places.

objects.idea: Tokenizers are unfair across languages: fertility, the tokens spent per word, differs.
objects.image: A toll booth that takes one coin a word from some travellers and two from others, for the same message.

formation.new: Vertical bars of tokens per word for several languages, from the module's fertility results.

objects.idea: Each token sends out a query; every token offers a key; the better a key lines up, the larger its weight.
objects.image: In the atrium each guest shines a torch; the others hold up mirrors, and the mirrors that face the torch flash brightest.

objects.idea: Attention is a soft dictionary lookup: the answer is the values weighted by those matches; the scores are divided by √d_head first, so the softmax does not saturate.
objects.image: The guest collects a cup from each mirror-holder and pours them together, more from the brightest.

objects.idea: The causal mask: each token reads only what came before it.
objects.image: Every seat in the atrium has blinkers so no guest can look at anyone who came in later.

objects.idea: Multi-head attention: each head learns its own habit, such as one step back.
objects.image: Several torches per guest, each with a coloured lens, each looking for a different kind of neighbour.

objects.idea: The block: attention, then a small MLP, each adding into the residual stream with pre-norm, repeated.
objects.image: The atrium repeats along the corridor like locks on a canal; at each, the guests and then a clerk tip a cupful into the blue channel, and it flows on.

objects.idea: A convolution slides a small kernel of weights over the image: locality and weight sharing.
objects.image: A stamp the size of a postage stamp walks across a mural, inking a weighted sum at each spot.

formation.new: A 20 × 21 point grid (the grid formation) with a 3 × 3 gold window sliding across it; the output grid fills point by point.

objects.idea: A small CNN invents its own edge and blob detectors with no one telling it to.
objects.image: The stamps on the door's shelf turn out, when you look, to be little edges and dots no one carved.

formation.new: Sixteen small 3 × 3 point patches that sharpen from noise into edge and blob patterns as training runs.

objects.idea: A ViT cuts the image into patches and reads them as tokens with the same block, without the causal mask.
objects.image: The picture is cut into square tiles, and the tiles walk in single file through the door into the atrium, where no one wears blinkers.

objects.idea: Attention maps show where the model looks: last-layer [CLS] attention and attention rollout.
objects.image: A lantern behind the picture lights up the parts the guests are staring at.

formation.new: The image grid with each point's size and colour set by its [CLS] attention weight.

objects.idea: CLIP matches images to text prompts with no task training; pretraining scale trades against task fine-tuning.
objects.image: Captions hang on hooks by the door; each picture walks to the caption nearest in meaning.

formation.new: One image point and several caption points on a sphere; the nearest caption lights gold.

objects.idea: Account for where every parameter lives in a real model: embeddings, attention and MLP, layer by layer.
objects.image: Thirty-two atria in a row; in each the torch-bearers fill one bench and the clerks of the small network fill three.

formation.new: 420 points shared out among boxes for the embedding table, then per-layer attention and MLP boxes in proportion to their parameter counts.

objects.idea: Tokens become points in a learned space; tokens used alike sit close: July beside June and August, before any layer runs.
objects.image: On the gallery floor, word-tiles cluster: months together, countries together, code together.

objects.idea: The model scores every token it knows; a softmax turns the scores into odds.
objects.image: From the balcony a row of flags rises over the garden, one per token, as tall as its odds.

objects.idea: Temperature, top-k, top-p and min-p reshape the odds before you sample.
objects.image: A wind on the balcony: cold, and only the tallest flag stands; warm, and the flags draw level.

objects.idea: The logit lens reads the residual stream at every layer through the output head; the answer settles at a decision layer.
objects.image: Windows along the gallery each show a flag; from one window on, they all show the same winner.

formation.new: A column of layer slices; at each slice a small bar chart of next-token odds; from one layer up the top bar stays gold.

objects.idea: A chat template wraps each turn in special tokens the model was trained on.
objects.image: Each speaker's words go in an envelope with a coloured seal at each end; the model learned to read from sealed letters.

objects.idea: Load a transformer from raw bytes: a manifest says where each tensor sits in one flat blob.
objects.image: A scribe unrolls one long scroll of numbers and snips it into labelled pieces.

formation.new: A long ribbon of points that splits into named blocks: embeddings, then per-layer QKV, MLP and norms.

objects.idea: The KV cache keeps each token's key and value, so decoding stays linear instead of quadratic.
objects.image: Shelves along the scriptorium wall where each written token leaves its key and value, never written twice.

objects.idea: Prefill pushes the prompt through to fill the cache; decode adds one token at a time, and there the mask has nothing to hide.
objects.image: The scribe first copies the page he was given, to stock his shelves, then writes on one letter at a time.

formation.new: An attention matrix whose lower triangle fills in one flash (prefill), then gains one row per step (decode) with no masked cells in the new row.

objects.idea: Sample by hand: temperature, top-k and top-p from scratch.
objects.image: A bag of letter tiles in proportion to the odds; the scribe trims the bag before drawing.

objects.idea: Quantise weights to int8 and weigh size against quality; GGUF's Q8_0 is the same idea, Q4_K a harsher one.
objects.image: Pens that write with only 255 shades of ink, and a ledger of what was lost.

objects.idea: A parity test: the hand-written engine must match PyTorch to the tolerance.
objects.image: Two scribes write the same page; laid one on the other, every letter lines up.

formation.new: Two point clouds that overlay exactly; any point that differs beyond the tolerance turns gold.

objects.idea: A GRU's update gate mixes the old state with a new candidate, token by token.
objects.image: A satchel with a flap that opens a little or a lot, mixing old contents with the new.

formation.new: One fixed cloud of points (the state); at each token a gate value blends it toward a new candidate cloud.

objects.idea: A recurrent model carries one fixed-size state instead of keeping every past token.
objects.image: Next door the shelves grow; here a single satchel of fixed size is all anyone carries.

objects.idea: A diagonal linear recurrence is a convolution, so it trains in parallel; check it against one token at a time.
objects.image: A row of fading footprints that can be stamped all at once or one step at a time, with the same result.

formation.new: A sequence of points whose state is a decayed sum of the past; drawn once as a sliding kernel and once step by step, overlapping.

objects.idea: Selective scan: when the decay depends on the input, the convolution is gone and a scan is needed.
objects.image: Each new footprint now decides how fast the old ones fade, so no single stamp fits the row and you must walk it step by step.

formation.new: The same sequence with a per-token decay that varies; the kernel picture breaks into a chain of steps.

objects.idea: Count and measure what each model keeps between tokens: the GPT's cache grows, the recurrence stays flat.
objects.image: A rising pile of books next to a satchel that never gets heavier.

formation.new: Two curves of memory per generated token against context length: a rising line and a flat one.

objects.idea: The state is a matrix S that stores values under keys: S k returns the value.
objects.image: A slate grid on the wall; touch a key at the head of a column and its value lights up down that column.

formation.new: A square grid of points (as in wgrid); a key column and the returned value row light blue.

objects.idea: Linear attention adds each pair into S; decay fades old pairs; both leave interference as S fills.
objects.image: Chalk written over chalk until the slate is grey; a damp cloth fades the oldest writing.

formation.new: Pairs written into the grid as outer products; the grid gets noisier; a decay factor dims older writes.

objects.idea: The delta rule writes by correcting: read what S returns for k and write only the gap to v; that is one step of gradient descent.
objects.image: Before writing, the clerk reads what the slate says under that key and chalks in only what is missing or wrong.

objects.idea: The gated delta rule adds decay to the delta rule; compute it a chunk at a time with one triangular solve.
objects.image: A clerk who chalks in only the difference and also wipes the whole slate a little before each write.

formation.new: The delta rule's grid with a global fade per step; the sequence split into chunks, each solved in one go.

objects.idea: Fill one 32 × 32 state past its size: plain adding keeps a little of every pair; the rules that correct or fade keep the newest and lose the oldest.
objects.image: One slate with more and more names chalked on; four clerks read them back, and the ones who rub out as they write lose the oldest names first.

formation.new: Recall curves against the number of stored pairs for each write rule, from the module's capacity results.

objects.idea: The forward process adds Gaussian noise on a schedule, and has a closed form that jumps to any step.
objects.image: A fog machine in the corner turns a spiral of lanterns into haze, one puff at a time.

objects.idea: Train a network to predict the noise that was added; one squared error is the whole loss.
objects.image: A guide in the fog points at each lantern and says how far the fog has pushed it.

objects.idea: Run it backwards: start from pure noise and subtract the predicted noise, step by step.
objects.image: The fog machine runs backwards, drawing the haze in puff by puff, until the spiral of lanterns stands clear.

objects.idea: Swap the scheduler, DDPM to DDIM, and trade steps for quality.
objects.image: The same clearing done in ten long strides instead of hundreds of small ones.

formation.new: Two reverse paths for the same points: many short steps against few long ones, ending close together.

objects.idea: Latent diffusion, text conditioning and classifier-free guidance turn a denoiser into Stable Diffusion.
objects.image: Whisper 'cat' to the guide: he clears the fog once with the word and once without, then steps further the way the word pulled.

formation.new: Reverse paths bent toward one labelled target cloud, more strongly as a guidance scale rises.

objects.idea: Flow matching regresses a straight-line velocity from noise to data; one sampling step lands on the average.
objects.image: Strings stretched straight from each noise point to a spiral point; cut to a single step, every point lands in the middle.

formation.new: Spiral data and noise points joined by straight lines; points move along them; a one-step sample collapses to the centre.

objects.idea: A masked diffusion model: drop the causal mask, hide a random share of characters, learn to guess them back.
objects.image: A line of blank tiles on a long table, filling in the surest letters first, in any order.

objects.idea: Sample a line in any number of steps; the reveal rule decides which blanks fill first.
objects.image: A dial on the table from 1 to 128; turned low, many letters appear at once and the line gets worse.

formation.new: The fill formation run at 1, 8 and 128 steps side by side.

objects.idea: Block diffusion writes block by block left to right, denoising inside each block, with a KV cache over finished blocks.
objects.image: The table is cut into short boards; each board fills by unmasking, then slides onto the scriptorium's shelf.

formation.new: Blocks of tiles left to right; within the current block tiles unmask; finished blocks drop into a cache row.

objects.idea: A data-repeat curve: on text seen 200 times the diffusion curve crosses under its overfitting twin, but the twin stopped at its best epoch still leads; on fresh data the twin leads throughout.
objects.image: Two runners on a looping track: the first peaks at lap 64 and tires; the second starts slowly and passes him at lap 200, but never beats his best lap.

formation.new: Two loss curves against epochs of repeated data; they cross.

objects.idea: Train one recipe at six sizes, from 51k to 3.2M parameters, and watch each held-out loss settle.
objects.image: Six footings poured side by side, each wider than the last, each with its own water mark.

objects.idea: Loss falls as a power of size: a straight line on log axes; check the fitter on known data first.
objects.image: A plumb line stretched across the footings that touches every water mark.

objects.idea: Count N by hand and compute C = 6ND for training.
objects.image: A brick counter: six times the bricks times the loads.

formation.new: A block of points N wide and D deep, stacked six layers high, its count shown as C.

objects.idea: Each compute budget has a best size; a toy grid can fake that optimum.
objects.image: A rope draped over the footings: the lowest point under each budget picks the size.

objects.idea: Kaplan and Chinchilla disagreed on how to split compute between size and data, and why.
objects.image: Two architects arguing over one plan, one adding floors, the other adding bricks to each floor.

formation.new: Two lines of optimal N against C with different slopes, crossing the module's toy points.

objects.idea: Supervised fine-tuning: next-token loss on curated replies, read with care.
objects.image: The tailor's tape measures only the sleeves, the replies, not the whole coat.

objects.idea: Full fine-tuning moves every weight.
objects.image: A whole coat unpicked and resewn, every stitch moved.

objects.idea: Most of the change lives in a few directions: the update has low intrinsic rank.
objects.image: Lay the changes side by side and they all point along a few seams.

objects.idea: LoRA trains two thin matrices beside a frozen one, under 3% of the weights.
objects.image: Two thin strips of cloth pinned beside the coat; the coat itself stays untouched.

objects.idea: LoRA's B starts at zero, so training starts from the unchanged model.
objects.image: The new strips start the same colour as the coat, so on day one nobody sees a change.

objects.idea: Forgetting is the rise of a held-out loss on the old task while learning a new one.
objects.image: Old books on a shelf whose ink fades as new books are pressed in beside them.

objects.idea: Measure how far the model moved as KL from the start model, and say on which inputs.
objects.image: A tape measure from each book's old spot to where it now stands.

formation.new: Points drift from their start positions; a faint line joins each to its start; the mean length is shown.

objects.idea: Replay and self-distillation keep most of the old skill; LoRA learns less and forgets less.
objects.image: Every few new books, someone reads aloud from an old one and its ink darkens again.

objects.idea: Compare methods at a matched new-task score, not only at the end; one number predicts forgetting only sometimes.
objects.image: Racers lined up at the same finishing post, so you compare what they dropped on the way.

formation.new: A scatter of runs: forgetting against new-task gain, with a vertical line at a matched gain.

objects.idea: Loss of plasticity: plain backprop can lose the ability to learn; continual backprop resets dead units.
objects.image: Some shelves go dusty and stop taking books; a caretaker swaps a few out for new ones.

formation.new: A grid of units that dim and go dark over tasks; a few are relit at each step.

objects.idea: Bradley-Terry: scores from pairwise choices; the chance one wins is a sigmoid of the score gap.
objects.image: Two glasses, a taster points at one; each glass's score shifts by the surprise.

objects.idea: Train a linear reward head on a frozen model and test it on held-out pairs.
objects.image: A scorecard clipped to a closed cask: the cask is never opened, only the card is learned.

objects.image: A rope from the hut back to the schoolhouse, paid out as the class changes.

objects.image: A plant that grows a fake ruler beside itself.

objects.idea: Read an evolve-set gain against a held-out gain; they differ.

objects.image: Plumb lines down the lens tower, and a second tower of random glass beside it.

route.why: Start at the far end of the old garden, at a line strung between two stakes: the first machine that learned fixed a line each time it was wrong.
A line needs training; next door, four tricks need little or none: count with Bayes, ask the neighbours, find the main axis, sum up with a few centres.

The string line stopped at the first cut that worked. The pond finds the widest one, lifts points so a flat cut works, keeps memories as valleys and shows the curve that dips twice. Its outflow is attention: follow it to the house, and go down the garden steps first.
Garden steps drop under the balcony, where the loss is computed. Learning starts there: the error is sent back through the graph, one local slope at a time.
Slopes alone train nothing: the mill turns them into a loop of batches, steps and measures, and shows the loss on unseen data turning up.
Unseen data has to stay unseen: beside the mill sits the vault, where splits, metrics, thresholds and leaks are kept honest.
With a fair score, watch how the optimiser moves: the floor sinks into a slope where step size, momentum and late understanding play out.
All of that used labels. In the blindfold room the data supplies its own: hide part, predict it, and stop the cheat where everything maps to one point.
Last room on the gradient's path: what if no gradient comes back at all? Learning with forward passes and local goals.
The stair rises beside the gate, the last place the gradient reaches. Now walk forwards: text arrives and is chopped into tokens.
Tokens become vectors and pour into the residual stream; in the atrium each one asks the others what to read.
Pictures skip the gate's merges: cut into patches at the south door, they walk into the same block, and nobody wears blinkers.
At the end of the row stands a real model, many atria deep; its last vector becomes odds over every token, read on the balcony.
From the balcony, turn back along the north row: the scriptorium writes one token, keeps its keys and values, and sends it back to the gate.
The scriptorium's shelves grow with every token; the satchel room carries a fixed-size state instead.
A fixed state must be written well: the slate room writes each value by correcting what the slate already returns.
Every room so far wrote one token after another. The fog room makes a whole picture at once, by removing noise step by step.
Bring that idea back to text: start from a line of blanks and fill the surest first. The stair core is next door.
You have seen the whole model. Before climbing, go down past the cellar to the footings: how big to build it for a budget.
Up to the first floor, where weights change after training: the tailor fits a trained model with thin extra matrices.
Every fitting costs something: on the fading shelf the old skill wears away while the new one is learned.
Instead of showing good replies, let people choose between two: the tasting room learns from choices.
A tuned model is still big: the press makes it smaller by teaching, cutting and rounding.
Rounding after training costs; the three-coin room trains with three values from the start, and rounds the cache too.
Up again: from here on no weight moves. At the example desk a frozen model learns a rule from examples in its prompt.
Examples help; spending more tokens helps too: the scratch room thinks out loud and takes a vote.
If words change the answer, tune the words: the sign-painter repaints the instruction and keeps what scores.
Some answers are not in the weights at all: the library fetches the right page and pastes it in.
Give the model tools and a loop: the workshop of hands acts, reads the result and acts again. Its door opens on the outside stair.
Down in the yard the world gives scores, not labels: pull levers, keep what pays, and do not move too fast.
Put a language model in the yard and let a program mark its answers: reward from a checker.
Keep the checker, freeze the model: the greenhouse breeds programs and keeps only what the checker passes.
Instead of trying moves in the world, try them in a model of it: the sand table plans before acting.
Build that model from pictures alone: the camera obscura plans inside what it learned from frames. Its back wall is the tower.
Climb to look inside. At the tower's foot, the map room shows the shape a trained network gives its input.
One floor up, listen to single parts of a running model: hooks, probes, swaps and neurons.
Single neurons mix many things; the dictionary room rewrites each state as a few directions from a long list.
Point the same tools at vision models and a JEPA, and ask what one unit or one probe can prove.
At the top, test every finding against a random copy, a second seed and a known truth. From the lookout the whole palace lies below: walk it again in your head.

landmarks.what: A channel of blue water down the ground-floor corridor from the gate to the balcony. Every ground-floor room has a door on it and pours in; from any room you can see it.
Directly below, in the cellar, a channel of gold water runs the other way, west. Grates in the ground-floor corridor show it.
The output balcony looks east over the old garden: you can see the string-line bed where the walk began, farthest away because it is oldest.
Steps from the garden go down under the balcony into the cellar: the loss is computed at the output, so learning starts beneath it.
The stair core stands beside the gate. The cellar stair comes up there because the gradient reaches the embedding table last; every upper floor is reached from where text enters.
The picture door opens south onto the yard path: images come from the world and skip the gate's merges: they are cut into patches instead.
A light well in the yard path looks down into the blindfold room (16): the JEPA objective below, the JEPA world models (25, 31) across the path.
The tailor's room floor is glass over the atrium: thin matrices are added above the frozen block.

The north row is one storey high with a skylight roof; from the first-floor gallery outside the three-coin room you look down through the skylight onto the scriptorium's KV shelves (07), which 28 also rounds.
The only way from the house's top floor to the yard is the outside stair from the workshop of hands: agents are where the model starts to act.
The tower stands at the south-west corner and is the tallest thing. From the lookout you see the whole roof, the yard and, far east, the garden: the place to rehearse the walk.

prologue.what: Before the first bower, the garden gate: 420 points in a loose field (a1), then a grid of numbers (a2), then two kinds of points and a first wrong line (a3, a4). It opens the walk the way the Moves page opens.

epilogue.what: At the top, the Moves page's last chapter: five ideas that kept coming back, each pointing at rooms below: hide and predict (16, 33), one local rule (01), lookup as a dot product (04, 21, 27), propose, score, keep (22, 34, 35), no number without its control (05a, 32).
